subject.title: feat(codex): config to disable or scope the native hook relay (#91009)

question: When a Codex approval policy is active, may `nativeHookRelay.events` intentionally omit `permission_request`, or must OpenClaw retain that relay (or otherwise warn and require an explicit unsafe override)?
rationale: This is a product and security-boundary contract: source plumbing and unit coverage cannot decide whether an operator-configured relay may bypass the approval/policy callback path.

options.title: Retain approval relay for scoped lists
options.body: Force-add `permission_request` whenever approvals are active, then add resolver and harness coverage for the scoped and disabled configurations.

options.title: Permit the documented explicit override
options.body: Keep the current event-list behavior, but make the reference documentation and UI hint unambiguous that omitting `permission_request` disables that native approval relay.

options.title: Pause the configuration surface
options.body: Land the narrower default-path optimization first and defer this override until maintainers choose the long-term policy model.

recommendation.title: Retain approval relay for scoped lists
recommendation.body: Force-add `permission_request` whenever approvals are active, then add resolver and harness coverage for the scoped and disabled configurations.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent relay-default proposal is the closest active work defining which native callbacks must remain present under normal Codex operation.
